title: Field runway crash kit — pilot escalation & sell-sprint notes
content:
PURPOSE:
Quick, portable crash kit for sellers and SEs running time-sensitive pilot/POCs where latency/cost regressions or quota issues threaten deal momentum. Focus: triage, scripted customer messaging, fast fallback lanes, and minimal tech asks we can reasonably do in a 24–72h squeeze.

TL;DR (3 lines for AEs/SDRs):
- If latency > target or errors spike during demo/pilot, switch traffic to a compatible lower-cost model variant (see fallback matrix) and enable prefix caching. Tell customer: ‘We’ve put a temporary performance guardrail in place while we investigate — no change to your data or credentials.’
- If unit cost runs > 2x expected on 95th percentile, pause non-critical batch jobs and enable short-term token quotas; offer a short analysis window for cost attribution.
- Use the one-page pilot checklist + canary config before each customer demo. Always copy #pilot-ops in Slack.

QUICK TRIAGE FLOW (playbook for SE/AE within first 60 minutes of report):
1) Capture: timestamp, route/model, region, customer-route-id, example request id.
2) Confirm impact: severity A (demo down), B (degraded latency/errors), C (cost drift).
3) Immediate mitigations (choose one):
   - Severity A/B: Reroute to lower-latency region or smaller sequence-length model; enable streaming chunking; set strict request timeout.
   - Cost drift: enforce per-call max tokens=200, enable caching on the customer route, pause background embeddings.
4) Notify customer: use script below.
5) Open incident in JIRA INF-XXXX and tag eng-serving-runtime + sre.
6) Follow-up: commit rollback decision and resolution ETA within 3 hours.

CUSTOMER-FACING SCRIPTS (pick & tweak):
- Opening (fast): ‘Hi — quick heads up: we’ve detected elevated latency on the route powering your pilot. We’re applying a temporary performance configuration that won’t affect your data. You may see slightly shorter responses while we stabilize; we’ll update within 3 hours.’
- Cost note: ‘We’re seeing token usage variance on a small subset of calls. We’ve applied a guard (max tokens) to avoid unexpected costs while we analyze. We’ll share an itemized trace in 24 hours.’
- Reassurance (enterprise): ‘This is isolated to the pilot’s routing profile. We can lock in predictable dedicated capacity if you want guaranteed throughput while we finish testing.’

TECH CHECKLIST (things SE runs, quick):
- Confirm model version and pinned-variant (model-name@commit).
- Check prefix/KV cache hit rate for customer route — if < 40%, enable aggressive prefix caching.
- Sequence distribution: is 95th percentile > expected? If yes, add token-limit per call.
- Batching settings: verify local concurrency and batch max size; reduce batch depth for latency-sensitive demos.
- GPU/backoff errors: capture GPU OOM traces, check node health and kernel-versions; escalate to infra if repeated.
- Region failover: toggle to nearest available region and validate latency (p95).

FALLBACK MODEL MATRIX (quick reference):
- prod-large-v2 -> fallback: prod-medium-v2 (same family, lower memory)
- redwood-llm-3b -> fallback: redwood-llm-1.3b-quant (quantized lower-cost)
- embeddings-high-acc -> fallback: embeddings-lite (lower cost, check perf on key queries)
Notes: Always validate output quality on 3 golden prompts before confirming to customer.

COST / NEGOTIATION POINTS FOR CUSTOMER (one-liners):
- ‘Short-term dedicated capacity reduces unit volatility — we can model a 30/60/90 day reserved plan to cap spend.’
- ‘Prefix caching and a small prompt refactor often cut token spend 20–40% with minimal UX change.’
- ‘We can schedule a focused cost audit and provide token-attribution within 48 hours.’

PILOT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (minimal set for go/no-go):
- Functional: Correctness on 3 golden tests and <2% hallucination on domain prompts.
- Performance: p95 latency <= SLA (customer-agreed) for 90% of production traffic in region.
- Cost: 95th percentile cost per 1k tokens within 1.5x estimated baseline.
- Ops: Rollout and rollback documented; on-call assigned for pilot windows.

SE/CS HANDOFF SCRIPT (what to copy into handoff note):
- Pilot name, contact, region, model variant, expected peak qps, demo windows, acceptance criteria, recent incidents (if any), mitigation toggles used (prefix caching, model fallback), JIRA INF id.

RUNBOOK: QUICK CHECKS TO SHARE WITH CUSTOMER (short bullets to send):
- Confirm region and expected sequence lengths for typical calls.
- Avoid passing large docs in single call during trial; prefer chunked requests.
- Use the smaller embedding model for near-real-time similarity tests.

SAMPLE 5-MIN CANVAS FOR CONSOLE WALKTHROUGH (what SE shows in demo):
- Console route view (traffic + latency p50/p95), model variant, cost-per-1000 tokens.
- Live toggles: token cap, fallback model selection, region reroute.
- Quick trace example: show an individual trace that maps to an error and how to inspect tokens.

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS (notes to self):
- Q: Can we automate a temporary model fallback via policy when p95>threshold? (work with runtime team)
- Q: Do we have a default guardrail template for token caps per customer? (prodops?)
- Need a short template for legal/contract when reserved capacity is proposed — loop in legal.

ACTION ITEMS (first 72h):
- SE: run prefix caching experiment for top-5 pilot routes (owner: Diego) — due 48h.
- Eng: implement a one-click model-fallback toggle in console (owner: Lucas, eng-serving-runtime) — scope/ETA in INF-1897.
- GTM: prepare a one-page reserved-capacity ROI example for pilot upsell (owner: Priya) — draft in 72h.

MEETING/DRY-RUN CHECKLIST (pre-demo, tick boxes):
- [ ] Route pinned to intended model variant
- [ ] Token caps set for demo account
- [ ] Canary trace and golden prompts validated
- [ ] Slack #pilot-ops invite sent to customer support rep

SAMPLE SLACK/EMAIL BLAST (internal, short):
- Slack: ‘@sre @eng-serving-runtime heads-up: Pilot AcmeCorp (region us-west1) experiencing p95 latency spike. Applying fallback and enabling prefix cache. JIRA INF-1897. SE: Samantha L.’
- Email to AE: ‘Sent mitigation; metro fallback in place; customer notified. Standby for 3-hour update.’

APPENDIX: QUICK LINKS & REFERENCES
- Pilot ops handbook (confluence): GF-2345
- Relevant Jira: INF-1897 (template incident)
- Example GitHub demo app: github.com/redwood/demo-pilot

NOTES TO SELF (messy, keep):
- Keep scripts short; customers hate long technical blurbs in initial notification.
- We should A/B test the ‘temporary guardrail’ language vs ‘we’ve adjusted the route’ — which reads better to CFOs?
- Follow-up: add an example email for CFO/procurement when cost-overrun is flagged.

END
